summary: The risk-off stance (confidence 0.45, as the PM quotes it) was built on SPY at 735.29, only 1.05% above its 200-day (727.64), after -2.7% over 5 days and -5.0% over 21 days, plus VIXY +14.2% over 5 days. The first session of the 5-day window went the other way. The account's SPY benchmark rose from 575.58 to 589.21 (about +2.4%), and VOO and VTI gained 2.4% and 2.5% on the day. SPY closed back well clear of the 200-day line, so the regime-line break I flagged did not happen on day one. The stance is graded on 5 sessions (not yet resolved), but SPY would need to give back roughly 3.4% over the next four sessions for risk-off to score as right, so I rate it as not holding up so far. The call's tilts worked better than its direction: Real Estate favoured (VNQ +1.6% on the day, 21d +7.14% in the packet), Technology avoided is untested here, and bonds were flat (BND +0.01%, IEF -0.12%). Staples did not behave as a shelter or a leader: WMT +0.06%, DPZ -0.03%, KR -0.67% on a +2.4% SPY day.
broken_theses: Risk-off / fragile-backdrop call: day one of the 5-day window was a roughly +2.4% SPY rebound, about 1.4 points above the +1% threshold that scores risk-on. It would take a roughly 3.4% drop over the remaining four sessions to turn this into a right call. Provisional until the 5-day grade lands.

Reading the 1.05% cushion over the 200-day as a near-term break risk: the gap widened rather than closed. I over-weighted the packet's -5.0% 21d and the VIXY rise and under-weighted how often a 5% drawdown into a held 200-day line bounces.
update: Track record is 5 right and 4 wrong out of 9 graded (hit rate 0.556), level with the 'always neutral' baseline of 0.556, so it adds nothing yet; both of my graded neutral calls (10-29, 10-30) were wrong on 5-day SPY returns of -4.7% and -2.7%, and risk-off now looks shaky on its first day. Lesson for next run: the packet is pre-open and stale by the time of the move, so a stance with confidence near 0.45 and a 200-day line only about 1% away is close to a coin flip. State what the packet shows about momentum after a sharp drop (21d -5.0%, 5d -2.7%) and do not let an event backdrop (hike odds, AI-capex worry) outweigh a still-intact trend (SPY above its 200-day, RSP 21d +1.97%, breadth better than the cap-weighted index). Watch the next close: SPY holding above 727.64 with VIXY falling favours moving to neutral or risk-on; a close below the line confirms the original risk-off view and turns off buys in code. L3 (staples not a shelter) was reinforced again today, one day only, not graded evidence.
